On a device with an SD card, side-loaded apps go in /meshcomod/apps/, not /apps/ at the root of the card; the SDK guide had it wrong, and it now also lists the input events apps really receive.
Polish (Polski) is in the Store's languages, translated by tom73god, and Settings > Language names a language added from the Store.
Arabic: letters join properly, Shift gives the Arabic 101 shift layer with the tashkeel, ك is on 8, ! $ @ type themselves and ? types ؟, and text leaves the device as standard Arabic letters, so a #channel name gives the same channel as on a phone (#582, thanks to jcyrio and a native-speaking helper).
Every new text is translated in all 14 languages, with wording fixes in Dutch, German and Hungarian (#632 and more by jcyrio), the new Pager texts in German (#755 by MrYoshii), and nineteen settings and messages that had no translation row, "Connections" among them.

The whole interface is redesigned: the status bar, Chats, the conversation screen, the lock screen, the screensaver, Home, Settings, notifications and the way text scales. Many things have moved, and the notes below say where they went.
Home is made of widgets now, and Glance is the layout you get after the update. Your old Home is still there as the Commander preset, in Settings > Display > Home.
Colour settings moved to a new Theme page: Appearance, High contrast, the accent colour, Colourful chat bubbles and Compact messages are no longer under Display. MORE COLORS! is switched on for everyone in its Regular style, and an aurora in your accent colour sits behind every screen; turn either off on the Theme page for a calmer look.
Settings backups made with beta_85 or earlier were written as invalid JSON and cannot be imported again. Make a fresh backup after updating: it is valid, carries the screen and app preferences the old ones were missing, and is named meshcore-backup-<date>.
Chat history on a busy device could stop saving without a word: once the history reached its 24 files, a reboot left every new message in memory only, gone at the next restart. Full files are now merged to make room, a new file is opened when they cannot be merged, and no message is ever dropped to keep saving. Messages lost that way before the update cannot be recovered.
T-Deck trackball: Scroll is the default now, and a trackball set to Cursor is moved to Scroll once by the update. Hold the trackball still for about half a second to switch between the two; a card in the middle of the screen says which one you are in.
The screensaver now also runs on battery, for 15 seconds after the screen timeout by default (Settings > Display > On battery, show it for). The old "Only while charging" option is gone; "Always on when connected to power" keeps it up while plugged in.
MeshCore 1.18 waits longer for a GPS to answer at start-up, so boards without a GPS take up to 5 seconds longer to boot. A device with no clock source starts from 1 March 2026 instead of May 2024.
Heltec V4: to make room for everything else, Snake is its only built-in game (2048, Tetris and Breakout are not built in), and it has no picture background, since a full-screen picture takes too much of its memory.
T-Display P4: landscape works. If beta_85 left your screen stuck in landscape with the controls out of reach, flash this build over USB from flasher.wadamesh.com. Taps were being rotated twice, once by the touch driver and once by the interface.
T-Display P4: if Wi-Fi never connects, your unit's Wi-Fi chip still runs LilyGo's factory firmware. Pick the "factory Wi-Fi chip" image in the flasher (#612, jalevdev spotted the missing choice in #619). If the board crashes with Wi-Fi on (within a minute of starting, or twice in half an hour), the next boot switches Wi-Fi off and says so; turn it back on in Settings to try again.
T-Deck Pro: there are now separate builds for the V1.0 and V1.1 hardware. A touchscreen that did nothing on some Pros was the wrong touch driver for that revision, and the build that matches your device fixes it. If you do not know which you have, take V1.1, which is what the single Pro build used to be; updating from the device keeps working without you choosing.
ThinkNode M9, Meshtastic edition: these newer units work. Their keyboard controller answers at a different address, so on beta_85 no key did anything and first setup could not be passed, and their GPS is switched on the other way round, which the firmware now picks from the keyboard's address (#662 by Bfindlay, reported in #644 by thejiraguy; #661 and #663 by Thatindianbruh).
Wio Tracker L2: the screen starts in landscape once after this update, now that it can rotate. The Orientation setting turns it back.
A failed SD card no longer costs your node its key: the device keeps a copy of the key in its own memory. A device that keeps its data on the card and starts without it says so and offers to try the card again, instead of opening first-time setup (reported on Discord).
One design across the whole firmware: one palette, a clear type scale (a light clock, SemiBold names, quieter secondary text), line icons everywhere, and one style for every switch, field, dropdown, checkbox, slider and button. The main action on a page is a solid teal button with dark text. The boot screen is animated: the mark lights up node by node and the wordmark rises into place.
The status bar is calmer: the clock in the middle, signal and battery on the right, unread messages on the left, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth small and grey. The scrolling node name stays on the Home tab. A GPS icon in the status bar: a grey crosshair while it searches, a lit pin once it has a position, and hidden while GPS is off.
Chats has All, Channels and Direct filters, a + to add a channel, and a menu with Mark all as read and Share my contact. The gear on every row is gone: hold a chat, or open the menu in the conversation header, for its options as a plain list of actions.
Every chat gets an icon drawn from its key, a square for a channel and a circle for a person. Under Theme you choose Glyphs or Initials (the first two letters in a coloured ball), and a chat icon you picked yourself still wins. A contact's chat with no icon of its own uses the first emoji in its name, and a text symbol such as a star or a heart can be picked as a chat icon (#640, an idea from jesshampshire; #647, reported by Jess-39).
The conversation header shows how the last message reached you: direct, a number of hops, or for a channel how many nodes it heard today. Each message says how many hops it came over, and your own channel posts say "Heard by N repeaters", counting the repeats as they come back.
A direct message shows Sent and then Delivered, the chats list shows the double tick as soon as it is delivered, and one that was not delivered says so and resends with a tap (reported by neoemit in #670).
Bubbles are neutral with the sender's colour on the name; Colourful bubbles colours the bubbles too, your own included, and mentions of you keep their blue bubble. The composer is a pill with a teal send button, and Emoji (and # on the ThinkNode M9) sit next to Send (#669 by oumike).
A new lock screen: the wadamesh mark, a large clock and the date, a line of mesh activity over the last 24 hours, up to two unread conversations, and the battery beside how to unlock. It moves a few pixels every minute so nothing burns in, and Settings > Lock screen > Message text on lock screen hides the text of those unread cards.
Messages that arrive in a chat you left open while the screen is off or locked stay unread, so the lock screen shows them; they count as read once you wake the device and see the chat (reported on Discord).
A new screensaver, Constellation: your node in the middle and the nodes you have heard around it, a ring wherever a packet came from, light along the routes of nodes heard in the last ten minutes, and quiet nodes fading out. It turns once an hour and drifts a few pixels against burn-in, and "Keep north up" stops the turn (#706, asked for by i-TomCZ). Settings > Display.
A message that arrives while the screen is dark shows as a notification card: the avatar, the conversation and sender, the hops, the time, how many have arrived and the message itself.
Settings opens on a grouped list with an icon for every page, starting with a Device page: what this unit is, its radio and hardware, and the About information, with Run setup again and Reboot. Display, Theme, Lock screen, Sound and Keyboard are grouped as Display & lock (#596 by oumike, asked for by Jess-39).
Every settings page uses the same cards and rows, and the control panel is drawn as square tiles coloured by their Settings group, filled while on, with a Battery saver tile. Hold the Settings tab to open it straight away.
Icon buttons say what they are: with a keyboard the selected button shows a small card after a moment, and on touch you hold a button to see it without tapping it. On a control panel tile, keep holding to open its settings. The keyboard cursor is amber, so the selected control stands out on every background.
The navigation bar can sit at the bottom, the top, the left or the right (Settings > Display > Navigation bar), as a rail on the sides. Condense Nav puts it on a rail on the right in landscape and shrinks the Home launchers to icons, so the content gets the full width; off by default.
Text wraps only at spaces, so a wrapped line no longer starts with a stray space after a comma or full stop. Button captions shrink, then wrap, when a translation is too wide for the button (#418, reported by B0N3-GD, built by oumike).
The Theme page opens on a preview of the launcher, a chat and the send button in what you pick, so you see the result before anything restarts. The mode, the accent and the colours wait for one Apply and restart button, which stays in reach in a slim bar under the title; the chat looks apply at once. Hold the theme chip in the control panel to open it.
MORE COLORS! comes in three styles with the layout unchanged. Regular gives every section its own colour and shows the status icons in colour; Neon is a near-black violet ground with electric cyan, hot magenta, laser yellow and acid lime and lit edges; Pastel is mint, baby blue, lavender, peach and rose on a warm dark ground.
Taste the rainbow gives every app, Settings page and tab its own place on the colour wheel and adds a little motion: the tab marker, the chats count and the focus ring travel round the wheel, buttons dip when pressed, and a new message lands with a flash of its sender's colour. The motion rests while the screen is off, locked or on the screensaver.
Names are always in colour, and in Day mode names and glyphs use a deeper shade so they read on white. High contrast keeps its own fixed colours, and the e-paper T-Deck Pro and Max show only the chat looks.
Backgrounds, under Settings > Theme > Background: the aurora, still or in a slow loop; a colour of your own; a picture (open a JPEG in Files and tap Set as background); or none. Cards and Home widgets are glass over it, and the Glass tiles switch draws them solid instead. The moving aurora only moves while you are not touching anything and stays still with the battery saver on.
A picture is darkened by day and lightened by night only as far as text needs to stay readable, and how far is yours to set: Picture dimming under Background and Wallpaper dimming under Lock screen, each Off, Light, Medium or Strong, with Strong as the default and today's look (asked for by zomgugoff and benanderson).
Lock screen > Default wallpaper takes you back from a picture of your own (#626, asked for by neoemit), and wallpapers and background pictures load on boards that keep files on SD_MMC or internal storage, such as the T-Display P4 (#691, reported by zomgugoff, fixed by oumike). A wallpaper in internal /lock/ survives a reboot: the start-up cleanup of old map tiles was deleting every picture on internal storage.
Home is widgets you arrange yourself: hold any widget to drag it, pick small, wide or large, add from the catalog, remove, and set its options. Each orientation keeps its own layout, and keypad boards arrange Home from Settings > Display > Home (the M9 can also hold Enter).
Start from a preset: Glance, Commander (the old Home, rebuilt from widgets), Radio, Minimal or Sensors.
Twenty-four widgets: clock, sun and moon, system, note, unread, chat, mentions, heard, nearest, remote sensor, radio, signal, airtime, GPS, position, battery, sensors (Expansion Kit), links, advert, app, switches and app widgets, plus a mesh radar on the 8 MB boards and a compass on the ThinkNode M9. Tapping a widget opens what it shows; the radar opens the radar screensaver until you touch the screen. Unread, Chat and Mentions have a large size that lists the messages themselves, and Mentions shows the message that names you and counts messages rather than chats.
Lua apps can put a widget on Home with wada.widget.set, on boards with the extended SDK; Airtime does.
wadamesh runs on MeshCore 1.18, through meshcomod v1.18.0.1, and Settings > About shows it under Build.
The MeshCore app's Command Line works with the device: name, Bluetooth PIN, Wi-Fi, radio settings, airtime and duty cycle, transmit power, receive gain, path hash mode, board and version. A contact you give remote CLI permission in the app can run those commands on your device over the mesh; anyone else's command arrives in the chat as a message.
Channel data, pushed sensor telemetry and raw sends over multi-byte paths reach the app as they do on MeshCore 1.18, and a device keeps its time through a restart that was not a power cut.
The Admin button on a repeater or room server opens a full admin app instead of a password box and a raw console. Log in as admin or guest (a remembered password logs in at once), then see its status, firmware and owner, its neighbours, telemetry and access list, change roles, identity, location, radio, repeating, limits, adverts, passwords and regions, and run an advert, a clock sync, neighbour discovery, a counter reset, a reboot or a firmware update. The old console stays under Advanced. The login password field says it takes up to 15 characters, which is all a MeshCore login carries.
Repeater telemetry and status requests answer far more often: the device asks directly first, the way the MeshCore app does, and only logs in when that gets no reply (#683, reported by 900steve).
A request to a node that never answers lets go of the device's single request slot after 45 seconds, instead of holding it until a reboot and leaving every later status, neighbour and access list empty (reported by enthusiastric).
The same touch interface runs at app.wadamesh.com and drives your own MeshCore node over USB or Bluetooth (Chrome or Edge), or a wadamesh or meshcomod node over Wi-Fi from wifi.app.wadamesh.com. It brings the map, the Store and Lua apps, backups and your device's location, keeps its chats in the browser, and works on phones in portrait. Without a node it runs a demo mesh. The web app has Reply on a channel message (#650 by oumike, asked for in #642 by Danie10), and the web remote shows real hop counts.
The device's own web interface refuses to send to a channel that went missing while you had it open, instead of falling back to the first channel on the device and sending there on the public channel with nothing on screen to say so (reported by TippyLion28).
Optional PIN lock: Settings > Lock screen > PIN lock asks for 4 numbers or letters, at boot and whenever the screen goes off. A forgotten PIN cannot be recovered, only reset along with everything on the device, and you accept a warning saying so before it is set. Every fifth wrong try makes you wait, from 30 seconds up to 4 minutes, and the count survives a reboot.
Keyboards type the PIN (a 0, or any digit on the Sym layer, included), touch-only boards get an on-screen pad, and the ThinkNode M9, T-LoRa Pager and Tanmatsu get a number pad you move through with the keys or the wheel (#676 by oumike, reported by TerryTel93 in #675). The Heltec V4, V4-R8, Attaky and CrowPanel boards have no lock screen and so no PIN.
Contacts can have a nickname: Contact options > Nickname. It shows wherever the contact appears (Contacts, Chats, sender names, the lock screen, notifications, Home widgets and the map) and stays on the device; the mesh, the phone app and Lua apps keep the real name, and Contacts search finds either.
Contacts has a Rooms filter, and Peers now lists people only (#740 by oumike, asked for by green.six and benanderson). The contact list shows each contact's chat icon (#649 by oumike, asked for in #646 by Jess-39). Contacts and Discovered can be sorted by Fewest hops (#718, asked for by mrickey, built by oumike), and A-Z sorts by name with Select all taking every contact that matches (#605).
Contacts can delete themselves when not heard from in a chosen number of days (Settings > Contact Management, off by default). Favourites and the open chat are never deleted, and nothing goes while the clock is not set (#731 by oumike, asked for in #719 by mrickey).
Hashtags in messages are links: tap #mesh, or select the message with keys, to open or join that channel. The message menu gains Map, Web and Channel entries for the coordinates, web addresses and hashtags in it (#580 by TerryTel93).
Emoji can go into any text field, not only a chat message: long-press the field and the picker sits alongside Cut, Copy, Paste and Sym, in Lua app text entry too. Emoji in a settings field are drawn instead of empty boxes (#690 by tun0).
Record your route: Map options > Record track saves a GPX file with elevation and time to /meshcomod/tracks on the SD card. It keeps recording with the screen off, the map draws the route as a red line, and the corner shows distance and climb (asked for on Discord).
Maps from one file: put a raster PMTiles archive in /maps on the SD card and pick it under Map options. Vector and JPEG archives are refused with the reason, and "Zoom: map levels only" keeps the map inside the levels the file has (#759 by kremers).
Offline maps fill the gaps: when a tile is missing and Wi-Fi is not connected, the map scales up the matching square from a tile one to three zoom levels above, so you see a blocky but correct map instead of an empty square, and you can zoom three levels past what you saved (asked for by benanderson).
Map options > Favorites only shows just your favourite contacts on the map, link lines included, and is remembered. The map's side buttons show which one is selected. Pick your advert position on the map instead of typing coordinates (#635 by Confituurke).
The Reader is a library: big text and markdown files on the SD card page through 16 KB at a time, and Files opens web pages and long texts in it. The desktop tool scripts/sdpack.py turns EPUB books and text files into pages with a library home page (asked for on Discord).
Settings > Display > Temperature in Fahrenheit shows °F everywhere temperatures appear; what is stored and sent stays in °C.
Orientation offers Portrait, Portrait 180, Landscape and Landscape 180 on every board that can rotate (#698, #701 by oumike). On large screens in landscape (T-Display P4, Tanmatsu, CrowPanel 5.0 and 10.1) the empty message box is one line tall and grows as you type.
Time zones: 25 more, from Central, South, East and West Africa, Egypt and Moscow to Singapore, Perth, Korea, Adelaide, New Zealand, Argentina, Mexico City and Newfoundland. The list runs west to east, and a Custom offset you set stays as it is (asked for by gadgeteerza).
USB Files (files.wadamesh.com over the USB cable) works on every board whose USB socket is the ESP32-S3's own, now including the T-LoRa Pager, Heltec V4-R8, RAK WisMesh Tap V2, Wio Tracker L2 and the T-Deck Pro and Max (asked for by Ender436). Uploads are about 30 times faster, around 120 KB/s to the SD card, because a reply no longer sits in the USB chip's buffer.
USB Files can put Lua apps on the device: drop a .lua or .json file into meshcomod/apps on the SD card and it shows up the next time you open the app drawer (asked for on Discord).
Backups are listed by their date, or "Default", instead of the file name (#741 by oumike), and a device without a set clock numbers its backups instead of overwriting an earlier one (#688 by oumike, for #686 reported by zomgugoff).
First-time setup keeps Bluetooth on and shows a switch for it (#416, by oumike).
A battery saver switch on every touch board, which now works with Bluetooth or Wi-Fi on: only a connected phone app or someone watching the web view holds it off. It also rests the GPS and keeps a moving background still.
GPS battery saver, in Settings > GPS > Battery: the GPS rests between position checks (every 2, 5, 15 or 30 minutes) and stays awake while the map, the GPS page or Discover is open. Boards with a GPS power switch turn it off, and a u-blox receiver such as the T-Deck Plus's is told to stop, so switching GPS off on the T-Deck saves power too.
GPS serial speed: the T-Deck and the ThinkNode M9 find their GPS's speed themselves with the new Auto choice, the default; a speed you pick is used as it is. On the T-LoRa Pager, T-Deck Pro and Max and T-Display P4 the setting says it is only where the search starts (#613, reported by D-Melhede).
Every internet time sync also reaches the clock chip on boards that have one (the ThinkNode M9), "Sync clock" asks the time server right away when Wi-Fi is on, and the cold-boot time sync over saved Wi-Fi is more reliable (#620; reported by gadgeteerza).
Settings > Clock & time keeps the "By hand" field in the zone you just picked, so Set clock after a zone change no longer moves the clock by the difference (#699, reported by zomgugoff).
Direct messages sent from the phone app retry properly: wadamesh took the app's retries for a resent copy, so nothing went out, flood fallback included, while the app was told the message had been flooded. The direct-send timeout also read a packed path byte as 76 hops instead of 12 (#636, guidokok traced it).
Nodes whose adverts came over 2 or 3 byte path hashes appear among the recently heard nodes, and the phone app's advert path request returns their whole path instead of a cut-off one; the packed path length was being compared as if it were a byte count.
Hop counts above 64 are gone from the Discovered list, the "auto-delete above N hops" setting no longer throws away nodes one hop away, and direct neighbours are recognised, now that the hop count is read apart from the hash size sharing its byte (#621, reported by jesshampshire).
Channel region scope applies to every way of sending, the phone app included (#614), and a message's region scope shows in its Info and under the bubble (#594, reported by DenRalle).
Firmware updates over Wi-Fi no longer stop at 0 percent and restart the device, and a dropped or stalled download picks up where it stopped, up to 3 times, instead of failing with "short read" (#689, reported by Hixsten).
Save update bin to SD downloads the file first, writes it to the card, closes it and checks it there before reporting success, and the SD health check keeps off the card meanwhile (#734, reported by Jess-39 and william-stearns).
Languages from the Store download on every board: the file is saved as it arrives instead of held in one big block of memory first, which the 2 MB Heltec V4 could not spare, and a file that is truly too large says so instead of blaming the server (reported by 161ct006).
The Store lists more than 16 apps, and its tile shows how many of your installed apps have an update waiting, found by the firmware update check. Store installs complete: a download is written in pieces, verified on the card and only then installed, so a failed install leaves nothing behind and a failed update keeps the old version. A cut-off download used to leave an app that failed with "syntax error near <eof>" (reported by halflive-743).
Wi-Fi after a lost link: the device's retry no longer races the Wi-Fi chip's own reconnect or clears the saved network, slows down after a minute so an absent network is not searched all night, and tries once at once when the screen wakes (#685, reported by william-stearns and stephen-62). Wi-Fi switched on from a Home widget or the control panel joins straight away.
Companion sync: a node keeps a sync position for up to 8 apps, and when all 8 are taken the slot of the app that synced longest ago is reused, instead of a new app never syncing at all.
Deleting a chat's history no longer makes the chat disappear from Chats, as the confirmation always promised; Delete chat removes it (by jcyrio).
A restore that cannot save identity, channels and contacts says so instead of restarting into an empty store (#708, reported by zomgugoff, built on #709 by oumike), and settings that fail to save to an SD slot file recreate the file and try again (#744 by oumike, #743).
Import backup shows your backups when there are two or more, and the time zone and Wi-Fi scan pages no longer open blank: the page was sized before it was laid out (#738 by oumike; #757, #760, reported by Ender436 and Kb1hux).
The "SD card could not be read" notice no longer appears when the card works, on devices that keep their data on internal storage after an unfinished copy to the card (#667, reported by 900steve).
The screen lock holds the trackball as well as the touchscreen, so the map no longer pans underneath a locked screen (#566 by samdems).
The control panel's clock keeps time while the panel is open (#666, reported by 900steve), and a settings page opened from it stays in front of the app drawer (#696, oumike).
Avatars never go blank: a name starting with a flag or joined emoji took an invisible character as its icon, and Initials skip emoji and take whole letters, so "ãna" shows ÃN (#674, reported by neoemit).
Characters a font cannot draw show as one "*" everywhere, skin-tone modifiers are hidden, and invisible marks in Arabic and Hebrew messages stay invisible (#679 by oumike, reported by neoemit in #673). Accented letters are the size of the text around them at the Large and Huge text sizes, and Romanian ș and ț are drawn instead of an empty box.
The contact popup is wider on 320 pixel screens and gives a long name a second line, so with Large Text it no longer runs under the buttons (reported by Danie10 in #668). The message info popup keeps its colours when a long repeater name wraps (#602, NewtsLament found the cause).
Leaving a profile field you did not edit no longer claims it saved, and scrolling that page no longer says "saved" on every row. A crash when tapping the accent popup after its text box had closed is fixed.
A slider drag is no longer cut off as a swipe, so the new value is saved; avatar initials fit their circle at large text sizes; and the on-screen keyboard's control and symbol keys are readable in dark mode (#656, oumike).
The browser opens the wadamesh changelog when there is no home page on the SD card and Wi-Fi is up, over plain http so the T-Deck Pro has the memory for it (#622, an idea from jesshampshire; #638). It is also at wadamesh.com/changelog.html.
Keypad navigation scrolls past text and charts: when the next control is further away than the screen shows, Up and Down move the page a step at a time first, so a long description or a chart between two buttons is seen before the cursor moves on (asked for by benanderson and zomgugoff).
When a new message rebuilds the chat list, the cursor stays on the same chat, so OK opens it instead of the Chats menu (ThinkNode M9, T-Deck trackball, T-LoRa Pager, Tanmatsu).
On the keypad boards (ThinkNode M9, Tanmatsu, T-LoRa Pager) a chat's settings, with Region & scope, are reached by moving up to the conversation header and pressing Enter (#623, reported by bobbythefett).
Up and Down on a web page scroll the text instead of jumping past it to the toolbar (#680 by oumike, reported by Buko84 in #677). The docs page on wadamesh.com has key guides for the ThinkNode M9, the T-Deck keyboard and the Tanmatsu.
Telemetry: the Request button is reachable with the keys while a history chart shows (reported by benanderson).
The interface fits the 480x222 panel with a one-row status bar. Shift and the knob set brightness or volume, holding Shift turns on Quiet now, holding Fn shows every shortcut, holding a letter picks its accent, the map zooms on the knob without going black, and Home shows the latest chat (#753 by MrYoshii).
Keyboard navigation with remappable tab keys, as on the T-Deck. M, C, A and S work from Home, hold H for the launcher options and S for the control panel, Backspace goes back when nothing is being typed, N jumps to the first new message, holding Enter is a long press, and Fn with Enter pastes the clipboard (#624 by jcyrio). Clicking the wheel on a slider adjusts it with the wheel.
Each tab remembers where you were, Contacts opens on the first contact, a chat opens on its first unread message, and Power off asks first. The screen draws quicker, tabs switch at once, and the keyboard is only read when a key is waiting.
The vibration motor buzzes for messages, with patterns and strength in Settings > Sound (#748 by MrYoshii).
The charger and fuel gauge show real charge, current and time to full or empty, with battery care (stop at 80%), a temperature guard and low-battery warnings that switch off safely at 3% (#749 by MrYoshii).
Power off is a real power-off (ship mode) when not on USB: hold the power key or plug in USB to start it again. It also sleeps the radio and switches off the GPS, the panel and the keyboard light, and Wi-Fi uses modem sleep while the screen is off (#750 by MrYoshii). Battery: the GPS rests in standby between position checks and is switched off completely when GPS is off, the display panel sleeps with the screen, and the speaker amplifier only runs while a sound plays.
The GPS gets the last position, and the time when the clock is known to be right, at power-up for a faster first fix, and stays awake three minutes after the map closes (#758 by MrYoshii).
The motion sensor keeps notifications quiet while the Pager lies face down, can wake the screen when you pick it up (opt-in), and Lua apps can read it (#751 by MrYoshii). The lock screen can have a wallpaper (#752 by MrYoshii).
The clock no longer loses about half an hour a day: the accurate clock chip is read back every hour instead of trusting the processor's own timer (diagnosed by jcyrio).
Map labels show their copyright sign and arrows instead of boxes, and the Secondary keyboards page names double-tap SPACE, which is what switches layout on the Pager, T-Deck Pro and Max (by jcyrio).
A slow key press that flickers on release types one letter, not two, and the same letter again is only taken after a moment that follows your typing pace (#625 and #671, reported by neoemit; #628 by oumike).
The notice icons along the bottom of the screen are gone; the status bar already shows unread messages, so they only repeated it over whatever was on screen.
The keyboard light has a brightness setting in Settings > Keyboard, like the T-Deck's (#664, asked for by Buko84).
MSG on the chat list opens Contacts, and MSG from Contacts goes back to Chats (#765, asked for by Eddie-Feher-at-TT). The d-pad cursor no longer lands on a message hidden under the text field when messages arrive (#764, reported by mrickey).
The back button behaves, chats and channels can all be marked read at once, the chat header fits its text (#627), and the battery percentage, 100 included, fits beside the signal bars at every text size (reported by buko84 and jd1227).
T-Deck: Settings > Display > UI size offers Normal, Large text and Huge text, applied after a restart, and the T-Deck Pro and Max have the same choice (#645 by oumike, asked for in #639 by Jess-39).
T-Deck: a damaged trackball that clicks and rolls by itself can be switched off (Settings > Keyboard > Navigation, "Use the trackball"). Space still locks, Enter on the lit lock screen unlocks or opens the PIN screen, and power off wakes only with the reset button (asked for on Discord).
T-Deck: an older keyboard that sends a burst like "QERUOXV$ ZNMFJ" for one Q is recognised, switched to the older keyboard setting and remembered.
T-Deck: with Italian, Spanish or Romanian selected, Sym+W, E and R type 1, 2 and 3 again; the accented letters come from the accent box after the base letter (#747, reported by QuakeRadio).
T-Deck Pro: Wi-Fi starts with Bluetooth on, now that the e-paper draw buffer is out of the scarce internal memory (#763, reported by oumike).
T-Deck Pro: Settings, the header, the chat composer, the lock screen and the boot screen fit and read well on the 240 px e-paper panel (#742 by oumike), and a slow boot no longer ends locked on the logo (#762, reported by oz1kfy).
T-Deck Pro and Max: the terminal is readable (it drew black text on black), compact chat messages no longer run into each other, and Lua apps draw correctly on e-paper (#704 by Ender436).
T-Deck Max: notification sounds, your own sounds and app audio play through its speaker (#665 by Ender436).
T-Display P4: support for the LR2021 radio variants, a clip-on keyboard, GPS that starts reliably, Wi-Fi through the C6 coprocessor, and a clock that syncs over saved Wi-Fi on a cold boot. Portrait screens that were cut off or overlapping are laid out properly.
T-Display P4: a one-row status bar with the title on the left and the clock beside the icons, and Settings in landscape in two real columns (by oumike).
T-Display P4: when the Wi-Fi chip stops answering (units on LilyGo's factory image lost Wi-Fi after about an hour), it is reset and rejoins the network on its own, no reboot needed (#685, reported by william-stearns).
T-Display P4 with the keyboard: the keyboard light and the screen backlight are separate, so the brightness slider only changes the screen and F11 only the keyboard light, which has its own setting in Settings > Keyboard (asked for by zomgugoff). The battery percentage comes from the voltage while the keyboard is attached (#722 by oumike, #721).
T-Display P4: Radio settings has "Always use the external antenna (MMCX)", which warns first, and the control panel has an Antenna tile. T-Display P4: vibrates on new messages with the AW86224 motor, off by default and quiet under Do Not Disturb (#730 by ItsNix).
T-Display P4: map tiles cache with no SD card, an SD card Launcher left in SPI mode is power-cycled and mounted at start-up (#708, built on #709 by oumike), and backup dates follow your time zone after a Wi-Fi sync (#756 by oumike).
P4 boards (T-Display P4, CrowPanel P4 10.1, Tanmatsu): a crash restarts the device instead of freezing on its last frame, which looked like a blue screen after boot, and the crash report is still saved.
New board: the Elecrow CrowPanel Advance 3.5 inch (by oumike).
New board: the Elecrow CrowPanel Advance 5.0 (#655 by oumike).
New board, experimental: the Elecrow CrowPanel Advanced 10.1 (ESP32-P4, 1024 by 600), one image per board revision (V1.0, V1.1, V1.2, printed on the board), with an SX1262 module in the wireless slot. Touch works, map tiles are kept on the board's own storage, and the time zone survives a Wi-Fi time sync (asked for on Discord).
New board: the SenseCAP Indicator D1L, with its ST7701S screen, FT6336 touch and the SX1262 radio behind the TCA9535 expander. Power off is hidden, as nothing on the board can wake it again, and the map says there is no map storage instead of asking to reflash a partition it does not have (#682 by Confituurke; #692, reported by skykingisepic).
Heltec V4: all translations are built in, compressed, with only the language you use unpacked, which gives it about 330 KB of room.
Heltec V4-R8: the Store's Apps tab is back, the chat bar buttons are easier to hit and a near miss no longer opens the control panel (#598, reported by Jess-39), and the 100 percent battery reading fits beside the signal bars.
Wio Tracker L2: the speaker plays notification chimes (#712, by oumike), and it gets the clock settings and boot time sync.
Attaky Mesh Deck: an Orientation setting so it runs in portrait, File Transfer to internal storage with Backup and Restore on the browser page, and no on-screen keyboard while the keyboard module is attached, which the Device page reports.
Screens draw faster: a frame takes fewer slices, the still aurora is drawn once and copied, and the drawing code is compiled for speed with its busiest loops in the chip's fast memory. On a T-Deck that is a third to a half more frames a second, with the same treatment on the M9, Attaky, RAK WisMesh Tap V2, Wio Tracker L2, CrowPanel 3.5 and V4-R8, and the T-LoRa Pager in fewer slices.
Spectrum is redesigned: tiles for the peak, the noise floor, your channel and how busy it is, a filled trace with a peak hold line, and a waterfall that stays dark until there is real signal. Band and Channel switch between the whole band and your channel up close, and Live, 1 min and 10 min set its history.
RF Monitor 1.4: tiles for RSSI, noise, margin and packets per minute, a signal chart, and the recently heard packets; select one for who sent it, its route, its margin above what your spreading factor can decode, its size and its time on the air.
Airtime 1.6: the channel load as a big figure, tiles for the average, the peak and your own time on the air, a chart with the duty-cycle limit, and the receive and transmit split, plus a Home widget.
Music plays the MP3 and WAV files in a Music folder on the SD card, with shuffle and repeat, and keeps playing with the screen off, on every board with a speaker: the T-Deck, T-LoRa Pager, T-Display P4, Tanmatsu and T-Deck Max. Store apps on the T-Display P4, the Tanmatsu and the Wio Tracker L2 can read the SD card and play music from it.
MECP posts emergency messages in the Mesh Emergency Communication Protocol: pick a severity and the codes, add the number of people and your position, and post it to a channel; MECP messages you receive are shown in plain words. MECP and its code table are by xiang-dev-1 (asked for on Discord).
Games: Tetris, Breakout, Space Invaders 1.1 (#707, #729 by JackCortines) and Blackjack 1.2.2 with split, double down and a bankroll kept between sessions (#681, #705 by halflive-743).
Outdoors: ProTreck 1.2 with a compass and three alarms, Trip Odometer 1.1 with return-to-home, and Ping, all by samuelcoustet; Wardrive 1.3 names what the next press of its start and stop button does (#735 by SebRut).
A Store app that changed a button's text could crash the device, and larger files saved with wada.fs.write could land cut off on the SD card; neither can happen now.
Lua apps no longer leak memory every time they redraw a screen: clearing a page released the widgets but kept the code attached to each, so an app slowed down and eventually could not draw, and a reused address could have made a new button run old code (reported by Jade).
Lua apps get a shared sending budget against spam that a restart does not refill: channel posts three in a row and then one a minute, direct messages six and then one every ten seconds, and the same text to the same channel twice within ten minutes is refused (#606, reported by TransientOddity).
wada.ui.emoji(cb) opens the emoji picker and returns the chosen emoji; wada.ui.input() fields already have it on their long-press menu. wada.ui.input takes an optional 4th argument, the longest text it accepts (up to 2000 characters, 63 without it), caps().input_len says the device has it, and Enter returns the text, from an external keyboard on a touch board too (asked for by rock.paper.scissors_).
wada.sys.epoch() and wada.sys.datetime() give the device clock, wada.sys.random(n) gives 1 to n, and random(1, 1) and a random over the full number range behave.
A Store app can ship its own files, such as sounds, listed in its manifest and installed into its own folder, which is also the way to play sounds on the T-Display P4.
Rounded panels, bold and large figures, button:bg(colour) for a button's own fill, and an event when a track ends that also arrives with the screen off. Canvases larger than 480 pixels are fitted to the screen instead of stopping the app.
On a device with an SD card, side-loaded apps go in /meshcomod/apps/, not /apps/ at the root of the card; the SDK guide had it wrong, and it now also lists the input events apps really receive.
Polish (Polski) is in the Store's languages, translated by tom73god, and Settings > Language names a language added from the Store.
Arabic: letters join properly, Shift gives the Arabic 101 shift layer with the tashkeel, ك is on 8, ! $ @ type themselves and ? types ؟, and text leaves the device as standard Arabic letters, so a #channel name gives the same channel as on a phone (#582, thanks to jcyrio and a native-speaking helper).
Every new text is translated in all 14 languages, with wording fixes in Dutch, German and Hungarian (#632 and more by jcyrio), the new Pager texts in German (#755 by MrYoshii), and nineteen settings and messages that had no translation row, "Connections" among them.

The whole interface is redesigned: the status bar, Chats, the conversation screen, the lock screen, the screensaver, Home, Settings, notifications and the way text scales. Many things have moved, and the notes below say where they went.
Home is made of widgets now, and Glance is the layout you get after the update. Your old Home is still there as the Commander preset, in Settings > Display > Home.
Colour settings moved to a new Theme page: Appearance, High contrast, the accent colour, Colourful chat bubbles and Compact messages are no longer under Display. MORE COLORS! is switched on for everyone in its Regular style, and an aurora in your accent colour sits behind every screen; turn either off on the Theme page for a calmer look.
Settings backups made with beta_85 or earlier were written as invalid JSON and cannot be imported again. Make a fresh backup after updating: it is valid, carries the screen and app preferences the old ones were missing, and is named meshcore-backup-<date>.
Chat history on a busy device could stop saving without a word: once the history reached its 24 files, a reboot left every new message in memory only, gone at the next restart. Full files are now merged to make room, a new file is opened when they cannot be merged, and no message is ever dropped to keep saving. Messages lost that way before the update cannot be recovered.
T-Deck trackball: Scroll is the default now, and a trackball set to Cursor is moved to Scroll once by the update. Hold the trackball still for about half a second to switch between the two; a card in the middle of the screen says which one you are in.
The screensaver now also runs on battery, for 15 seconds after the screen timeout by default (Settings > Display > On battery, show it for). The old "Only while charging" option is gone; "Always on when connected to power" keeps it up while plugged in.
MeshCore 1.18 waits longer for a GPS to answer at start-up, so boards without a GPS take up to 5 seconds longer to boot. A device with no clock source starts from 1 March 2026 instead of May 2024.
Heltec V4: to make room for everything else, Snake is its only built-in game (2048, Tetris and Breakout are not built in), and it has no picture background, since a full-screen picture takes too much of its memory.
T-Display P4: landscape works. If beta_85 left your screen stuck in landscape with the controls out of reach, flash this build over USB from flasher.wadamesh.com. Taps were being rotated twice, once by the touch driver and once by the interface.
T-Display P4: if Wi-Fi never connects, your unit's Wi-Fi chip still runs LilyGo's factory firmware. Pick the "factory Wi-Fi chip" image in the flasher (#612, jalevdev spotted the missing choice in #619). If the board crashes with Wi-Fi on (within a minute of starting, or twice in half an hour), the next boot switches Wi-Fi off and says so; turn it back on in Settings to try again.
T-Deck Pro: there are now separate builds for the V1.0 and V1.1 hardware. A touchscreen that did nothing on some Pros was the wrong touch driver for that revision, and the build that matches your device fixes it. If you do not know which you have, take V1.1, which is what the single Pro build used to be; updating from the device keeps working without you choosing.
ThinkNode M9, Meshtastic edition: these newer units work. Their keyboard controller answers at a different address, so on beta_85 no key did anything and first setup could not be passed, and their GPS is switched on the other way round, which the firmware now picks from the keyboard's address (#662 by Bfindlay, reported in #644 by thejiraguy; #661 and #663 by Thatindianbruh).
Wio Tracker L2: the screen starts in landscape once after this update, now that it can rotate. The Orientation setting turns it back.
A failed SD card no longer costs your node its key: the device keeps a copy of the key in its own memory. A device that keeps its data on the card and starts without it says so and offers to try the card again, instead of opening first-time setup (reported on Discord).
One design across the whole firmware: one palette, a clear type scale (a light clock, SemiBold names, quieter secondary text), line icons everywhere, and one style for every switch, field, dropdown, checkbox, slider and button. The main action on a page is a solid teal button with dark text. The boot screen is animated: the mark lights up node by node and the wordmark rises into place.
The status bar is calmer: the clock in the middle, signal and battery on the right, unread messages on the left, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth small and grey. The scrolling node name stays on the Home tab. A GPS icon in the status bar: a grey crosshair while it searches, a lit pin once it has a position, and hidden while GPS is off.
Chats has All, Channels and Direct filters, a + to add a channel, and a menu with Mark all as read and Share my contact. The gear on every row is gone: hold a chat, or open the menu in the conversation header, for its options as a plain list of actions.
Every chat gets an icon drawn from its key, a square for a channel and a circle for a person. Under Theme you choose Glyphs or Initials (the first two letters in a coloured ball), and a chat icon you picked yourself still wins. A contact's chat with no icon of its own uses the first emoji in its name, and a text symbol such as a star or a heart can be picked as a chat icon (#640, an idea from jesshampshire; #647, reported by Jess-39).
The conversation header shows how the last message reached you: direct, a number of hops, or for a channel how many nodes it heard today. Each message says how many hops it came over, and your own channel posts say "Heard by N repeaters", counting the repeats as they come back.
A direct message shows Sent and then Delivered, the chats list shows the double tick as soon as it is delivered, and one that was not delivered says so and resends with a tap (reported by neoemit in #670).
Bubbles are neutral with the sender's colour on the name; Colourful bubbles colours the bubbles too, your own included, and mentions of you keep their blue bubble. The composer is a pill with a teal send button, and Emoji (and # on the ThinkNode M9) sit next to Send (#669 by oumike).
A new lock screen: the wadamesh mark, a large clock and the date, a line of mesh activity over the last 24 hours, up to two unread conversations, and the battery beside how to unlock. It moves a few pixels every minute so nothing burns in, and Settings > Lock screen > Message text on lock screen hides the text of those unread cards.
Messages that arrive in a chat you left open while the screen is off or locked stay unread, so the lock screen shows them; they count as read once you wake the device and see the chat (reported on Discord).
A new screensaver, Constellation: your node in the middle and the nodes you have heard around it, a ring wherever a packet came from, light along the routes of nodes heard in the last ten minutes, and quiet nodes fading out. It turns once an hour and drifts a few pixels against burn-in, and "Keep north up" stops the turn (#706, asked for by i-TomCZ). Settings > Display.
A message that arrives while the screen is dark shows as a notification card: the avatar, the conversation and sender, the hops, the time, how many have arrived and the message itself.
Settings opens on a grouped list with an icon for every page, starting with a Device page: what this unit is, its radio and hardware, and the About information, with Run setup again and Reboot. Display, Theme, Lock screen, Sound and Keyboard are grouped as Display & lock (#596 by oumike, asked for by Jess-39).
Every settings page uses the same cards and rows, and the control panel is drawn as square tiles coloured by their Settings group, filled while on, with a Battery saver tile. Hold the Settings tab to open it straight away.
Icon buttons say what they are: with a keyboard the selected button shows a small card after a moment, and on touch you hold a button to see it without tapping it. On a control panel tile, keep holding to open its settings. The keyboard cursor is amber, so the selected control stands out on every background.
The navigation bar can sit at the bottom, the top, the left or the right (Settings > Display > Navigation bar), as a rail on the sides. Condense Nav puts it on a rail on the right in landscape and shrinks the Home launchers to icons, so the content gets the full width; off by default.
Text wraps only at spaces, so a wrapped line no longer starts with a stray space after a comma or full stop. Button captions shrink, then wrap, when a translation is too wide for the button (#418, reported by B0N3-GD, built by oumike).
The Theme page opens on a preview of the launcher, a chat and the send button in what you pick, so you see the result before anything restarts. The mode, the accent and the colours wait for one Apply and restart button, which stays in reach in a slim bar under the title; the chat looks apply at once. Hold the theme chip in the control panel to open it.
MORE COLORS! comes in three styles with the layout unchanged. Regular gives every section its own colour and shows the status icons in colour; Neon is a near-black violet ground with electric cyan, hot magenta, laser yellow and acid lime and lit edges; Pastel is mint, baby blue, lavender, peach and rose on a warm dark ground.
Taste the rainbow gives every app, Settings page and tab its own place on the colour wheel and adds a little motion: the tab marker, the chats count and the focus ring travel round the wheel, buttons dip when pressed, and a new message lands with a flash of its sender's colour. The motion rests while the screen is off, locked or on the screensaver.
Names are always in colour, and in Day mode names and glyphs use a deeper shade so they read on white. High contrast keeps its own fixed colours, and the e-paper T-Deck Pro and Max show only the chat looks.
Backgrounds, under Settings > Theme > Background: the aurora, still or in a slow loop; a colour of your own; a picture (open a JPEG in Files and tap Set as background); or none. Cards and Home widgets are glass over it, and the Glass tiles switch draws them solid instead. The moving aurora only moves while you are not touching anything and stays still with the battery saver on.
A picture is darkened by day and lightened by night only as far as text needs to stay readable, and how far is yours to set: Picture dimming under Background and Wallpaper dimming under Lock screen, each Off, Light, Medium or Strong, with Strong as the default and today's look (asked for by zomgugoff and benanderson).
Lock screen > Default wallpaper takes you back from a picture of your own (#626, asked for by neoemit), and wallpapers and background pictures load on boards that keep files on SD_MMC or internal storage, such as the T-Display P4 (#691, reported by zomgugoff, fixed by oumike). A wallpaper in internal /lock/ survives a reboot: the start-up cleanup of old map tiles was deleting every picture on internal storage.
Home is widgets you arrange yourself: hold any widget to drag it, pick small, wide or large, add from the catalog, remove, and set its options. Each orientation keeps its own layout, and keypad boards arrange Home from Settings > Display > Home (the M9 can also hold Enter).
Start from a preset: Glance, Commander (the old Home, rebuilt from widgets), Radio, Minimal or Sensors.
Twenty-four widgets: clock, sun and moon, system, note, unread, chat, mentions, heard, nearest, remote sensor, radio, signal, airtime, GPS, position, battery, sensors (Expansion Kit), links, advert, app, switches and app widgets, plus a mesh radar on the 8 MB boards and a compass on the ThinkNode M9. Tapping a widget opens what it shows; the radar opens the radar screensaver until you touch the screen. Unread, Chat and Mentions have a large size that lists the messages themselves, and Mentions shows the message that names you and counts messages rather than chats.
Lua apps can put a widget on Home with wada.widget.set, on boards with the extended SDK; Airtime does.
wadamesh runs on MeshCore 1.18, through meshcomod v1.18.0.1, and Settings > About shows it under Build.
The MeshCore app's Command Line works with the device: name, Bluetooth PIN, Wi-Fi, radio settings, airtime and duty cycle, transmit power, receive gain, path hash mode, board and version. A contact you give remote CLI permission in the app can run those commands on your device over the mesh; anyone else's command arrives in the chat as a message.
Channel data, pushed sensor telemetry and raw sends over multi-byte paths reach the app as they do on MeshCore 1.18, and a device keeps its time through a restart that was not a power cut.
The Admin button on a repeater or room server opens a full admin app instead of a password box and a raw console. Log in as admin or guest (a remembered password logs in at once), then see its status, firmware and owner, its neighbours, telemetry and access list, change roles, identity, location, radio, repeating, limits, adverts, passwords and regions, and run an advert, a clock sync, neighbour discovery, a counter reset, a reboot or a firmware update. The old console stays under Advanced. The login password field says it takes up to 15 characters, which is all a MeshCore login carries.
Repeater telemetry and status requests answer far more often: the device asks directly first, the way the MeshCore app does, and only logs in when that gets no reply (#683, reported by 900steve).
A request to a node that never answers lets go of the device's single request slot after 45 seconds, instead of holding it until a reboot and leaving every later status, neighbour and access list empty (reported by enthusiastric).
The same touch interface runs at app.wadamesh.com and drives your own MeshCore node over USB or Bluetooth (Chrome or Edge), or a wadamesh or meshcomod node over Wi-Fi from wifi.app.wadamesh.com. It brings the map, the Store and Lua apps, backups and your device's location, keeps its chats in the browser, and works on phones in portrait. Without a node it runs a demo mesh. The web app has Reply on a channel message (#650 by oumike, asked for in #642 by Danie10), and the web remote shows real hop counts.
The device's own web interface refuses to send to a channel that went missing while you had it open, instead of falling back to the first channel on the device and sending there on the public channel with nothing on screen to say so (reported by TippyLion28).
Optional PIN lock: Settings > Lock screen > PIN lock asks for 4 numbers or letters, at boot and whenever the screen goes off. A forgotten PIN cannot be recovered, only reset along with everything on the device, and you accept a warning saying so before it is set. Every fifth wrong try makes you wait, from 30 seconds up to 4 minutes, and the count survives a reboot.
Keyboards type the PIN (a 0, or any digit on the Sym layer, included), touch-only boards get an on-screen pad, and the ThinkNode M9, T-LoRa Pager and Tanmatsu get a number pad you move through with the keys or the wheel (#676 by oumike, reported by TerryTel93 in #675). The Heltec V4, V4-R8, Attaky and CrowPanel boards have no lock screen and so no PIN.
Contacts can have a nickname: Contact options > Nickname. It shows wherever the contact appears (Contacts, Chats, sender names, the lock screen, notifications, Home widgets and the map) and stays on the device; the mesh, the phone app and Lua apps keep the real name, and Contacts search finds either.
Contacts has a Rooms filter, and Peers now lists people only (#740 by oumike, asked for by green.six and benanderson). The contact list shows each contact's chat icon (#649 by oumike, asked for in #646 by Jess-39). Contacts and Discovered can be sorted by Fewest hops (#718, asked for by mrickey, built by oumike), and A-Z sorts by name with Select all taking every contact that matches (#605).
Contacts can delete themselves when not heard from in a chosen number of days (Settings > Contact Management, off by default). Favourites and the open chat are never deleted, and nothing goes while the clock is not set (#731 by oumike, asked for in #719 by mrickey).
Hashtags in messages are links: tap #mesh, or select the message with keys, to open or join that channel. The message menu gains Map, Web and Channel entries for the coordinates, web addresses and hashtags in it (#580 by TerryTel93).
Emoji can go into any text field, not only a chat message: long-press the field and the picker sits alongside Cut, Copy, Paste and Sym, in Lua app text entry too. Emoji in a settings field are drawn instead of empty boxes (#690 by tun0).
Record your route: Map options > Record track saves a GPX file with elevation and time to /meshcomod/tracks on the SD card. It keeps recording with the screen off, the map draws the route as a red line, and the corner shows distance and climb (asked for on Discord).
Maps from one file: put a raster PMTiles archive in /maps on the SD card and pick it under Map options. Vector and JPEG archives are refused with the reason, and "Zoom: map levels only" keeps the map inside the levels the file has (#759 by kremers).
Offline maps fill the gaps: when a tile is missing and Wi-Fi is not connected, the map scales up the matching square from a tile one to three zoom levels above, so you see a blocky but correct map instead of an empty square, and you can zoom three levels past what you saved (asked for by benanderson).
Map options > Favorites only shows just your favourite contacts on the map, link lines included, and is remembered. The map's side buttons show which one is selected. Pick your advert position on the map instead of typing coordinates (#635 by Confituurke).
The Reader is a library: big text and markdown files on the SD card page through 16 KB at a time, and Files opens web pages and long texts in it. The desktop tool scripts/sdpack.py turns EPUB books and text files into pages with a library home page (asked for on Discord).
Settings > Display > Temperature in Fahrenheit shows °F everywhere temperatures appear; what is stored and sent stays in °C.
Orientation offers Portrait, Portrait 180, Landscape and Landscape 180 on every board that can rotate (#698, #701 by oumike). On large screens in landscape (T-Display P4, Tanmatsu, CrowPanel 5.0 and 10.1) the empty message box is one line tall and grows as you type.
Time zones: 25 more, from Central, South, East and West Africa, Egypt and Moscow to Singapore, Perth, Korea, Adelaide, New Zealand, Argentina, Mexico City and Newfoundland. The list runs west to east, and a Custom offset you set stays as it is (asked for by gadgeteerza).
USB Files (files.wadamesh.com over the USB cable) works on every board whose USB socket is the ESP32-S3's own, now including the T-LoRa Pager, Heltec V4-R8, RAK WisMesh Tap V2, Wio Tracker L2 and the T-Deck Pro and Max (asked for by Ender436). Uploads are about 30 times faster, around 120 KB/s to the SD card, because a reply no longer sits in the USB chip's buffer.
USB Files can put Lua apps on the device: drop a .lua or .json file into meshcomod/apps on the SD card and it shows up the next time you open the app drawer (asked for on Discord).
Backups are listed by their date, or "Default", instead of the file name (#741 by oumike), and a device without a set clock numbers its backups instead of overwriting an earlier one (#688 by oumike, for #686 reported by zomgugoff).
First-time setup keeps Bluetooth on and shows a switch for it (#416, by oumike).
A battery saver switch on every touch board, which now works with Bluetooth or Wi-Fi on: only a connected phone app or someone watching the web view holds it off. It also rests the GPS and keeps a moving background still.
GPS battery saver, in Settings > GPS > Battery: the GPS rests between position checks (every 2, 5, 15 or 30 minutes) and stays awake while the map, the GPS page or Discover is open. Boards with a GPS power switch turn it off, and a u-blox receiver such as the T-Deck Plus's is told to stop, so switching GPS off on the T-Deck saves power too.
GPS serial speed: the T-Deck and the ThinkNode M9 find their GPS's speed themselves with the new Auto choice, the default; a speed you pick is used as it is. On the T-LoRa Pager, T-Deck Pro and Max and T-Display P4 the setting says it is only where the search starts (#613, reported by D-Melhede).
Every internet time sync also reaches the clock chip on boards that have one (the ThinkNode M9), "Sync clock" asks the time server right away when Wi-Fi is on, and the cold-boot time sync over saved Wi-Fi is more reliable (#620; reported by gadgeteerza).
Settings > Clock & time keeps the "By hand" field in the zone you just picked, so Set clock after a zone change no longer moves the clock by the difference (#699, reported by zomgugoff).
Direct messages sent from the phone app retry properly: wadamesh took the app's retries for a resent copy, so nothing went out, flood fallback included, while the app was told the message had been flooded. The direct-send timeout also read a packed path byte as 76 hops instead of 12 (#636, guidokok traced it).
Nodes whose adverts came over 2 or 3 byte path hashes appear among the recently heard nodes, and the phone app's advert path request returns their whole path instead of a cut-off one; the packed path length was being compared as if it were a byte count.
Hop counts above 64 are gone from the Discovered list, the "auto-delete above N hops" setting no longer throws away nodes one hop away, and direct neighbours are recognised, now that the hop count is read apart from the hash size sharing its byte (#621, reported by jesshampshire).
Channel region scope applies to every way of sending, the phone app included (#614), and a message's region scope shows in its Info and under the bubble (#594, reported by DenRalle).
Firmware updates over Wi-Fi no longer stop at 0 percent and restart the device, and a dropped or stalled download picks up where it stopped, up to 3 times, instead of failing with "short read" (#689, reported by Hixsten).
Save update bin to SD downloads the file first, writes it to the card, closes it and checks it there before reporting success, and the SD health check keeps off the card meanwhile (#734, reported by Jess-39 and william-stearns).
Languages from the Store download on every board: the file is saved as it arrives instead of held in one big block of memory first, which the 2 MB Heltec V4 could not spare, and a file that is truly too large says so instead of blaming the server (reported by 161ct006).
The Store lists more than 16 apps, and its tile shows how many of your installed apps have an update waiting, found by the firmware update check. Store installs complete: a download is written in pieces, verified on the card and only then installed, so a failed install leaves nothing behind and a failed update keeps the old version. A cut-off download used to leave an app that failed with "syntax error near <eof>" (reported by halflive-743).
Wi-Fi after a lost link: the device's retry no longer races the Wi-Fi chip's own reconnect or clears the saved network, slows down after a minute so an absent network is not searched all night, and tries once at once when the screen wakes (#685, reported by william-stearns and stephen-62). Wi-Fi switched on from a Home widget or the control panel joins straight away.
Companion sync: a node keeps a sync position for up to 8 apps, and when all 8 are taken the slot of the app that synced longest ago is reused, instead of a new app never syncing at all.
Deleting a chat's history no longer makes the chat disappear from Chats, as the confirmation always promised; Delete chat removes it (by jcyrio).
A restore that cannot save identity, channels and contacts says so instead of restarting into an empty store (#708, reported by zomgugoff, built on #709 by oumike), and settings that fail to save to an SD slot file recreate the file and try again (#744 by oumike, #743).
Import backup shows your backups when there are two or more, and the time zone and Wi-Fi scan pages no longer open blank: the page was sized before it was laid out (#738 by oumike; #757, #760, reported by Ender436 and Kb1hux).
The "SD card could not be read" notice no longer appears when the card works, on devices that keep their data on internal storage after an unfinished copy to the card (#667, reported by 900steve).
The screen lock holds the trackball as well as the touchscreen, so the map no longer pans underneath a locked screen (#566 by samdems).
The control panel's clock keeps time while the panel is open (#666, reported by 900steve), and a settings page opened from it stays in front of the app drawer (#696, oumike).
Avatars never go blank: a name starting with a flag or joined emoji took an invisible character as its icon, and Initials skip emoji and take whole letters, so "ãna" shows ÃN (#674, reported by neoemit).
Characters a font cannot draw show as one "*" everywhere, skin-tone modifiers are hidden, and invisible marks in Arabic and Hebrew messages stay invisible (#679 by oumike, reported by neoemit in #673). Accented letters are the size of the text around them at the Large and Huge text sizes, and Romanian ș and ț are drawn instead of an empty box.
The contact popup is wider on 320 pixel screens and gives a long name a second line, so with Large Text it no longer runs under the buttons (reported by Danie10 in #668). The message info popup keeps its colours when a long repeater name wraps (#602, NewtsLament found the cause).
Leaving a profile field you did not edit no longer claims it saved, and scrolling that page no longer says "saved" on every row. A crash when tapping the accent popup after its text box had closed is fixed.
A slider drag is no longer cut off as a swipe, so the new value is saved; avatar initials fit their circle at large text sizes; and the on-screen keyboard's control and symbol keys are readable in dark mode (#656, oumike).
The browser opens the wadamesh changelog when there is no home page on the SD card and Wi-Fi is up, over plain http so the T-Deck Pro has the memory for it (#622, an idea from jesshampshire; #638). It is also at wadamesh.com/changelog.html.
Keypad navigation scrolls past text and charts: when the next control is further away than the screen shows, Up and Down move the page a step at a time first, so a long description or a chart between two buttons is seen before the cursor moves on (asked for by benanderson and zomgugoff).
When a new message rebuilds the chat list, the cursor stays on the same chat, so OK opens it instead of the Chats menu (ThinkNode M9, T-Deck trackball, T-LoRa Pager, Tanmatsu).
On the keypad boards (ThinkNode M9, Tanmatsu, T-LoRa Pager) a chat's settings, with Region & scope, are reached by moving up to the conversation header and pressing Enter (#623, reported by bobbythefett).
Up and Down on a web page scroll the text instead of jumping past it to the toolbar (#680 by oumike, reported by Buko84 in #677). The docs page on wadamesh.com has key guides for the ThinkNode M9, the T-Deck keyboard and the Tanmatsu.
Telemetry: the Request button is reachable with the keys while a history chart shows (reported by benanderson).
The interface fits the 480x222 panel with a one-row status bar. Shift and the knob set brightness or volume, holding Shift turns on Quiet now, holding Fn shows every shortcut, holding a letter picks its accent, the map zooms on the knob without going black, and Home shows the latest chat (#753 by MrYoshii).
Keyboard navigation with remappable tab keys, as on the T-Deck. M, C, A and S work from Home, hold H for the launcher options and S for the control panel, Backspace goes back when nothing is being typed, N jumps to the first new message, holding Enter is a long press, and Fn with Enter pastes the clipboard (#624 by jcyrio). Clicking the wheel on a slider adjusts it with the wheel.
Each tab remembers where you were, Contacts opens on the first contact, a chat opens on its first unread message, and Power off asks first. The screen draws quicker, tabs switch at once, and the keyboard is only read when a key is waiting.
The vibration motor buzzes for messages, with patterns and strength in Settings > Sound (#748 by MrYoshii).
The charger and fuel gauge show real charge, current and time to full or empty, with battery care (stop at 80%), a temperature guard and low-battery warnings that switch off safely at 3% (#749 by MrYoshii).
Power off is a real power-off (ship mode) when not on USB: hold the power key or plug in USB to start it again. It also sleeps the radio and switches off the GPS, the panel and the keyboard light, and Wi-Fi uses modem sleep while the screen is off (#750 by MrYoshii). Battery: the GPS rests in standby between position checks and is switched off completely when GPS is off, the display panel sleeps with the screen, and the speaker amplifier only runs while a sound plays.
The GPS gets the last position, and the time when the clock is known to be right, at power-up for a faster first fix, and stays awake three minutes after the map closes (#758 by MrYoshii).
The motion sensor keeps notifications quiet while the Pager lies face down, can wake the screen when you pick it up (opt-in), and Lua apps can read it (#751 by MrYoshii). The lock screen can have a wallpaper (#752 by MrYoshii).
The clock no longer loses about half an hour a day: the accurate clock chip is read back every hour instead of trusting the processor's own timer (diagnosed by jcyrio).
Map labels show their copyright sign and arrows instead of boxes, and the Secondary keyboards page names double-tap SPACE, which is what switches layout on the Pager, T-Deck Pro and Max (by jcyrio).
A slow key press that flickers on release types one letter, not two, and the same letter again is only taken after a moment that follows your typing pace (#625 and #671, reported by neoemit; #628 by oumike).
The notice icons along the bottom of the screen are gone; the status bar already shows unread messages, so they only repeated it over whatever was on screen.
The keyboard light has a brightness setting in Settings > Keyboard, like the T-Deck's (#664, asked for by Buko84).
MSG on the chat list opens Contacts, and MSG from Contacts goes back to Chats (#765, asked for by Eddie-Feher-at-TT). The d-pad cursor no longer lands on a message hidden under the text field when messages arrive (#764, reported by mrickey).
The back button behaves, chats and channels can all be marked read at once, the chat header fits its text (#627), and the battery percentage, 100 included, fits beside the signal bars at every text size (reported by buko84 and jd1227).
T-Deck: Settings > Display > UI size offers Normal, Large text and Huge text, applied after a restart, and the T-Deck Pro and Max have the same choice (#645 by oumike, asked for in #639 by Jess-39).
T-Deck: a damaged trackball that clicks and rolls by itself can be switched off (Settings > Keyboard > Navigation, "Use the trackball"). Space still locks, Enter on the lit lock screen unlocks or opens the PIN screen, and power off wakes only with the reset button (asked for on Discord).
T-Deck: an older keyboard that sends a burst like "QERUOXV$ ZNMFJ" for one Q is recognised, switched to the older keyboard setting and remembered.
T-Deck: with Italian, Spanish or Romanian selected, Sym+W, E and R type 1, 2 and 3 again; the accented letters come from the accent box after the base letter (#747, reported by QuakeRadio).
T-Deck Pro: Wi-Fi starts with Bluetooth on, now that the e-paper draw buffer is out of the scarce internal memory (#763, reported by oumike).
T-Deck Pro: Settings, the header, the chat composer, the lock screen and the boot screen fit and read well on the 240 px e-paper panel (#742 by oumike), and a slow boot no longer ends locked on the logo (#762, reported by oz1kfy).
T-Deck Pro and Max: the terminal is readable (it drew black text on black), compact chat messages no longer run into each other, and Lua apps draw correctly on e-paper (#704 by Ender436).
T-Deck Max: notification sounds, your own sounds and app audio play through its speaker (#665 by Ender436).
T-Display P4: support for the LR2021 radio variants, a clip-on keyboard, GPS that starts reliably, Wi-Fi through the C6 coprocessor, and a clock that syncs over saved Wi-Fi on a cold boot. Portrait screens that were cut off or overlapping are laid out properly.
T-Display P4: a one-row status bar with the title on the left and the clock beside the icons, and Settings in landscape in two real columns (by oumike).
T-Display P4: when the Wi-Fi chip stops answering (units on LilyGo's factory image lost Wi-Fi after about an hour), it is reset and rejoins the network on its own, no reboot needed (#685, reported by william-stearns).
T-Display P4 with the keyboard: the keyboard light and the screen backlight are separate, so the brightness slider only changes the screen and F11 only the keyboard light, which has its own setting in Settings > Keyboard (asked for by zomgugoff). The battery percentage comes from the voltage while the keyboard is attached (#722 by oumike, #721).
T-Display P4: Radio settings has "Always use the external antenna (MMCX)", which warns first, and the control panel has an Antenna tile. T-Display P4: vibrates on new messages with the AW86224 motor, off by default and quiet under Do Not Disturb (#730 by ItsNix).
T-Display P4: map tiles cache with no SD card, an SD card Launcher left in SPI mode is power-cycled and mounted at start-up (#708, built on #709 by oumike), and backup dates follow your time zone after a Wi-Fi sync (#756 by oumike).
P4 boards (T-Display P4, CrowPanel P4 10.1, Tanmatsu): a crash restarts the device instead of freezing on its last frame, which looked like a blue screen after boot, and the crash report is still saved.
New board: the Elecrow CrowPanel Advance 3.5 inch (by oumike).
New board: the Elecrow CrowPanel Advance 5.0 (#655 by oumike).
New board, experimental: the Elecrow CrowPanel Advanced 10.1 (ESP32-P4, 1024 by 600), one image per board revision (V1.0, V1.1, V1.2, printed on the board), with an SX1262 module in the wireless slot. Touch works, map tiles are kept on the board's own storage, and the time zone survives a Wi-Fi time sync (asked for on Discord).
New board: the SenseCAP Indicator D1L, with its ST7701S screen, FT6336 touch and the SX1262 radio behind the TCA9535 expander. Power off is hidden, as nothing on the board can wake it again, and the map says there is no map storage instead of asking to reflash a partition it does not have (#682 by Confituurke; #692, reported by skykingisepic).
Heltec V4: all translations are built in, compressed, with only the language you use unpacked, which gives it about 330 KB of room.
Heltec V4-R8: the Store's Apps tab is back, the chat bar buttons are easier to hit and a near miss no longer opens the control panel (#598, reported by Jess-39), and the 100 percent battery reading fits beside the signal bars.
Wio Tracker L2: the speaker plays notification chimes (#712, by oumike), and it gets the clock settings and boot time sync.
Attaky Mesh Deck: an Orientation setting so it runs in portrait, File Transfer to internal storage with Backup and Restore on the browser page, and no on-screen keyboard while the keyboard module is attached, which the Device page reports.
Screens draw faster: a frame takes fewer slices, the still aurora is drawn once and copied, and the drawing code is compiled for speed with its busiest loops in the chip's fast memory. On a T-Deck that is a third to a half more frames a second, with the same treatment on the M9, Attaky, RAK WisMesh Tap V2, Wio Tracker L2, CrowPanel 3.5 and V4-R8, and the T-LoRa Pager in fewer slices.
Spectrum is redesigned: tiles for the peak, the noise floor, your channel and how busy it is, a filled trace with a peak hold line, and a waterfall that stays dark until there is real signal. Band and Channel switch between the whole band and your channel up close, and Live, 1 min and 10 min set its history.
RF Monitor 1.4: tiles for RSSI, noise, margin and packets per minute, a signal chart, and the recently heard packets; select one for who sent it, its route, its margin above what your spreading factor can decode, its size and its time on the air.
Airtime 1.6: the channel load as a big figure, tiles for the average, the peak and your own time on the air, a chart with the duty-cycle limit, and the receive and transmit split, plus a Home widget.
Music plays the MP3 and WAV files in a Music folder on the SD card, with shuffle and repeat, and keeps playing with the screen off, on every board with a speaker: the T-Deck, T-LoRa Pager, T-Display P4, Tanmatsu and T-Deck Max. Store apps on the T-Display P4, the Tanmatsu and the Wio Tracker L2 can read the SD card and play music from it.
MECP posts emergency messages in the Mesh Emergency Communication Protocol: pick a severity and the codes, add the number of people and your position, and post it to a channel; MECP messages you receive are shown in plain words. MECP and its code table are by xiang-dev-1 (asked for on Discord).
Games: Tetris, Breakout, Space Invaders 1.1 (#707, #729 by JackCortines) and Blackjack 1.2.2 with split, double down and a bankroll kept between sessions (#681, #705 by halflive-743).
Outdoors: ProTreck 1.2 with a compass and three alarms, Trip Odometer 1.1 with return-to-home, and Ping, all by samuelcoustet; Wardrive 1.3 names what the next press of its start and stop button does (#735 by SebRut).
A Store app that changed a button's text could crash the device, and larger files saved with wada.fs.write could land cut off on the SD card; neither can happen now.
Lua apps no longer leak memory every time they redraw a screen: clearing a page released the widgets but kept the code attached to each, so an app slowed down and eventually could not draw, and a reused address could have made a new button run old code (reported by Jade).
Lua apps get a shared sending budget against spam that a restart does not refill: channel posts three in a row and then one a minute, direct messages six and then one every ten seconds, and the same text to the same channel twice within ten minutes is refused (#606, reported by TransientOddity).
wada.ui.emoji(cb) opens the emoji picker and returns the chosen emoji; wada.ui.input() fields already have it on their long-press menu. wada.ui.input takes an optional 4th argument, the longest text it accepts (up to 2000 characters, 63 without it), caps().input_len says the device has it, and Enter returns the text, from an external keyboard on a touch board too (asked for by rock.paper.scissors_).
wada.sys.epoch() and wada.sys.datetime() give the device clock, wada.sys.random(n) gives 1 to n, and random(1, 1) and a random over the full number range behave.
A Store app can ship its own files, such as sounds, listed in its manifest and installed into its own folder, which is also the way to play sounds on the T-Display P4.
Rounded panels, bold and large figures, button:bg(colour) for a button's own fill, and an event when a track ends that also arrives with the screen off. Canvases larger than 480 pixels are fitted to the screen instead of stopping the app.
On a device with an SD card, side-loaded apps go in /meshcomod/apps/, not /apps/ at the root of the card; the SDK guide had it wrong, and it now also lists the input events apps really receive.
Polish (Polski) is in the Store's languages, translated by tom73god, and Settings > Language names a language added from the Store.
Arabic: letters join properly, Shift gives the Arabic 101 shift layer with the tashkeel, ك is on 8, ! $ @ type themselves and ? types ؟, and text leaves the device as standard Arabic letters, so a #channel name gives the same channel as on a phone (#582, thanks to jcyrio and a native-speaking helper).
Every new text is translated in all 14 languages, with wording fixes in Dutch, German and Hungarian (#632 and more by jcyrio), the new Pager texts in German (#755 by MrYoshii), and nineteen settings and messages that had no translation row, "Connections" among them.
